title: Two steps: benzene to phenylamine
caption: No single reaction puts –NH₂ on benzene. Nitration (concentrated HNO₃ and H₂SO₄, below 55 °C) gives nitrobenzene; reduction with tin and HCl, then NaOH, gives phenylamine.
alt: Benzene, arrow (conc. HNO₃, conc. H₂SO₄, 55 °C), nitrobenzene, arrow (Sn, HCl; then NaOH), phenylamine.
description: Step 2: C₆H₅NO₂ + 6[H] → C₆H₅NH₂ + 2H₂O, the [H] from tin and acid.
